definition_zh: 使工业化；发展工业；（国家或地区）实现工业化
definition_en: to develop industry in a country or area, so that more goods are made in factories by machines
core_image: 一片农田边立起厂房，烟囱冒出第一缕白烟
scene: 小镇原本靠种田和打铁为生，后来开了几家工厂。The little town began to industrialise when the first factories opened.
sceneCN: 这里 industrialise 是「使工业化、发展工业」（第 1 个义项：让工业成为当地主要生产方式）；句意：第一家工厂开张后，小镇开始工业化。

pos.zh: 使工业化；发展工业
（国家、地区）实现工业化

derivatives.zh: 由 industrialise 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「工业化」，结果名词
由 industry 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「工业的；产业的」
由过去分词转为形容词，义为「已工业化的」
由 industrial 加指人后缀 -ist 构成，义为「工业家；实业家」
加前缀 de-（去除）构成，义为「去工业化，减少工业比重」

senses.title: To make industry the main form of production
senses.definition: to change a country or region by building factories and using machines instead of hand work
senses.definitionCN: 通过建工厂、用机器代替手工，改变一个国家或地区的生产方式
senses.example: The government wanted to industrialise the northern provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 政府想让北方各省工业化。
senses.why: Industry once meant steady work, and later factory production, so to industrialise is to make that the main way of working.
senses.whyCN: industry 最初指持续的努力劳作，后来指工厂生产；把它变成主要工作方式，就是使工业化。

senses.title: To become an industrial country
senses.definition: of a country or region, to develop a large factory-based economy over time
senses.definitionCN: 指国家或地区逐步形成以工厂为基础的庞大经济
senses.example: Japan began to industrialise in the late nineteenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 日本在十九世纪后期开始实现工业化。
senses.why: The same word is used without an object, where the subject itself is the one that changes.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词也可以不带宾语，此时发生变化的就是主语国家本身。

senses.title: To put a process into machine production
senses.definition: to make a particular production process run in factories with machinery
senses.definitionCN: 使某项生产工艺在工厂里由机器批量完成
senses.example: Farmers were forced to industrialise their dairy business.
senses.exampleCN: 奶农被迫把乳业生产工业化。
senses.why: When the object is a branch of work rather than a country, industrialise means turning that work into factory production.
senses.whyCN: 当宾语不是国家而是某个行业时，industrialise 指把该行业的劳作改由工厂批量完成。

senses.title: Industrialised as a description
senses.definition: used of a place or economy that already has a lot of industry, as in a newly industrialised country
senses.definitionCN: 用于修饰已有大量工业的地方或经济体，如「新兴工业化国家」
senses.example: Singapore is often called a newly industrialised economy.
senses.exampleCN: 新加坡常被称为新兴工业化经济体。
senses.why: The past participle became an adjective, so a finished change can be used as a label on the place.
senses.whyCN: 过去分词转作形容词，于是已经完成的变化可以当作标签贴在地方上。

intro.en: Industrialise comes from industry, from Latin industria, active effort, plus the verb-forming suffix -ise.
intro.cn: industrialise 来自 industry，而 industry 源自拉丁语 industria（勤奋、努力），再加上构成动词的后缀 -ise。

items.en: Industria means diligence and activity.
items.cn: industria 意为勤奋、积极做事。

items.en: The word enters English through French as industry, first meaning diligence or skill.
items.cn: 该词经法语进入英语作 industry，最初义为勤奋或技艺。

items.en: With the growth of factories, industry comes to mean organised manufacturing.
items.cn: 随着工厂兴起，industry 逐渐指有组织的制造业。

items.en: Industrial describes what belongs to manufacturing.
items.cn: 派生形容词 industrial 指属于制造业的。

items.en: Industrialise carries both the effort sense and the factory sense into a verb.
items.cn: industrialise 把「努力」与「工厂」两层意思都带进了动词。

note.en: Industrialise belongs to the industry word family and sits near terms about economic change.
note.cn: industrialise 属于 industry 词族，并与描述经济变化的词相邻。

entries.definition: the American spelling of the same verb
entries.definitionCN: 同一动词的美式拼写
工业的；产业的
勤劳的；勤奋的

entries.definition: to make something more modern, often by new machines
entries.definitionCN: 使现代化，常指换用新机器

entries.definition: to use machines instead of people or animals
entries.definitionCN: 使机械化

entries.definition: to make an area more city-like
entries.definitionCN: 使城市化

normalIntro.en: Industrialise is industry turned into a verb: to make industry grow.
normalIntro.cn: industrialise 就是把 industry 变成动词：让工业生长起来。

normal.en: It is industry plus -ise, the verb ending that means to make.
normal.cn: 它由 industry 加表示「使……化」的动词后缀 -ise 构成。

normal.en: The noun is industrialisation, the country is industrialised, the adjective is industrial.
normal.cn: 名词是 industrialisation，国家是 industrialised，形容词是 industrial。

normal.en: British writing often uses the -ise ending, while American writing prefers -ize.
normal.cn: 英式写法多用 -ise 词尾，美式写法多用 -ize。

normal.en: A newly industrialised country is one that has just built up its factories.
normal.cn: newly industrialised country 指刚刚建起工厂体系的国家。

normal.en: The Latin root industria means effort, so industry still carries the idea of hard work.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 industria 意为努力，所以 industry 里仍然藏着苦干的意思。

abstract.en: Picture chimneys rising like new trees across a quiet field.
abstract.cn: 想象一根根烟囱像新树一样从安静田野里长出来。

abstract.en: Imagine hundreds of hands slowly replaced by hundreds of turning wheels.
abstract.cn: 想象成百上千双手慢慢被成百上千个转动的轮子取代。

abstract.en: Picture a map that turns from green fields to grey blocks over a hundred years.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图在百年间从绿色田野变成灰色街区。

examples.en: Many Asian economies began to industrialise after the war.
examples.cn: 许多亚洲经济体在战后开始工业化。

examples.en: The country was industrialised within two generations.
examples.cn: 这个国家在两代人的时间里实现了工业化。

examples.en: Air pollution rose in the heavily industrialised south.
examples.cn: 工业化程度很高的南方空气污染加重了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因打石子赖子」——村民们靠打石子、做砖块谋生，村子渐渐变得工厂林立；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 industria（勤奋、活动）→ 古法语 industrie → 英语 industry（勤奋；工业）→ industrial（工业的）→ industrialise（使工业化）；这个词根的核心是「持续的努力劳作」，义项则由「努力」逐步转向「工厂化的生产」。

sensesIntro.en: Industrialise moves from changing a place into factory work, to a country growing factories on its own, to making one trade machine-made, and finally to the adjective use for already changed places.
sensesIntro.cn: industrialise 先指把一个地方改造成工厂生产，再指国家自身发展工厂，接着指让某个行业机械化生产，最后指「已工业化的」这一形容词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: factory chimneys rising beside a green field.
core.cn: 核心意象：工厂烟囱在绿色田野边升起。

branches.en: Changing a place into a factory economy is the central transitive sense.
branches.cn: 把一个地方改造成工厂经济，是核心的及物义项。

branches.en: A country growing factories by itself is the intransitive sense.
branches.cn: 国家自身长起工厂，是不及物义项。

branches.en: Making one trade machine-made extends the change to a single industry.
branches.cn: 让某个行业机械化生产，是把变化缩小到单一行业。

branches.en: The participle as adjective labels places where the change is finished.
branches.cn: 分词转形容词，用来标出变化已经完成的地方。

branches.en: Factory work and country change share the same image of wheels replacing hands.
branches.cn: 工厂化生产与国家变革共享同一个画面：轮子取代双手。

intro.en: Industrialise is built from the industry word family plus the verb suffix -ise.
intro.cn: industrialise 由 industry 词族加上动词后缀 -ise 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin industria, effort or diligence, is the base of industry and of every word built on it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 industria（勤奋、努力）是 industry 及由此构成的所有词的基础。

items.example: Industria is the deepest layer of the word.
items.exampleCN: industria 是这个词最深的一层。

items.example: Industry keeps both the factory sense and the effort sense.
items.exampleCN: industry 同时保留工厂义与努力义。

items.example: The suffix -al forms industrial.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 industrial。

items.example: Industrial growth brought more jobs.
items.exampleCN: 工业增长带来更多工作。

items.example: The suffix -ise forms industrialise.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ise 构成 industrialise。

items.example: Industrialise turns the adjective into an action.
items.exampleCN: industrialise 把形容词变成动作。

items.meaningCN: 过程或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms industrialisation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 industrialisation。

items.example: Industrialisation changed the whole region.
items.exampleCN: 工业化改变了整个地区。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms industrialist.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ist 构成 industrialist。

items.example: The prefix de- forms deindustrialise.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 de- 构成 deindustrialise。

definition_en: working hard and steadily, and often keeping busy with useful tasks
core_image: 天还没亮就有人起身干活，手上一直不闲
scene: 邻家阿姨每天清早起来做针线活，晚上还在收拾院子。My neighbour is an industrious woman who is always busy with something useful.
sceneCN: 这里 industrious 是「勤劳的、勤奋的」（第 1 个义项：肯出力、长时间坚持劳作）；句意：我的邻居是个勤劳的女人，总在忙些有用的事。

pos.zh: 勤劳的；勤奋的；勤勉的

derivatives.zh: 由 industrious 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「勤勉地」
由 industrious 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「勤勉」
同根名词，古代主要指「勤奋」，现代主要指「工业」

senses.title: Working hard at everyday tasks
senses.definition: keeping steadily busy with work, and not avoiding effort
senses.definitionCN: 持续忙着做事，不躲避付出的力气
senses.example: She was a quiet and industrious woman.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个安静而勤劳的女人。
senses.why: The Latin adjective industrius means diligent, and that work sense still sits at the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁形容词 industrius 意为勤勉，这层「卖力做事」的意思至今仍在词的中心。

senses.title: Studying or training with care
senses.definition: putting steady effort into lessons, research, or practice
senses.definitionCN: 对待功课、研究或训练持续投入心力
senses.example: Industrious students rarely miss an early lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 勤奋的学生很少缺早课。
senses.why: Once hard work is the core, the same word easily points at learning, where effort shows in time and patience.
senses.whyCN: 既然核心是苦干，这个词也自然指向学习，因为学习中的努力体现在时间和耐心上。

senses.title: Describing busy animals or machines
senses.titleCN: 忙碌不闲的（动物、机器等）
senses.definition: used informally for animals or machines that are always busy doing something
senses.definitionCN: 口语中形容动物或机器总是忙个不停
senses.example: The industrious ants carried crumbs all day.
senses.exampleCN: 那些勤快的蚂蚁整天搬运面包屑。
senses.why: The word can leave the human world, as long as the busy pattern of steady work is still there.
senses.whyCN: 只要那种不停歇的忙碌模样还在，这个词就能走出人的世界，用在别的对象上。

senses.title: Slightly formal praise
senses.definition: a mildly formal way of praising someone as a dependable hard worker
senses.definitionCN: 略带正式色彩地称赞一个人踏实肯干、值得信赖
senses.example: The old craftsman was praised as an industrious man.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老匠人被称赞为勤恳之人。
senses.why: Because the word comes from Latin and feels a little old-fashioned, it often reads as careful praise rather than casual talk.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个词来自拉丁语、带点年代感，它常读作郑重其事的夸奖，而不是随口闲聊。

intro.en: Industrious comes from Latin industrius, diligent, formed in the shadow of Latin industria, effort.
intro.cn: industrious 来自拉丁语 industrius（勤勉的），它是在拉丁语 industria（努力）的影子下形成的形容词。

items.en: Industria means diligence and active effort.
items.cn: industria 意为勤奋与积极努力。

items.en: The adjective industrius describes a diligent person; some scholars link it to indu, within, but the detail is uncertain.
items.cn: 形容词 industrius 形容勤勉的人；有学者把它与 indu（在内）联系起来，但细节存疑。

items.en: Industrious appears in English meaning hard-working and clever at making things.
items.cn: industrious 在十六世纪进入英语，指肯出力、也善于做东西。

items.en: The word settles on steady hard work, while the noun industry begins to mean organised manufacturing.
items.cn: 这个词固定表示踏实的苦干，而名词 industry 开始指有组织的制造业。

items.en: Industrialise grows from the factory sense of industry, so the two words now look alike but point at different things.
items.cn: industrialise 由 industry 的工厂义发展而来，所以两个词形式相近，却指向不同的东西。

note.en: Industrious belongs to the industria family but has kept the effort sense, unlike industrial words about factories.
note.cn: industrious 属于 industria 家族，却保留了「努力」这层意义，与谈工厂的 industrial 类词不同。

entries.definitionCN: 与工厂、制造业有关的
工业；也可指勤奋

entries.definition: too willing to let someone have what they want
entries.definitionCN: 纵容的；溺爱的；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: showing steady, careful effort in work or study
entries.definitionCN: 勤勉的；用功的

entries.definition: putting a lot of effort into work
entries.definitionCN: 努力工作的；勤劳的

entries.definition: unwilling to work or use energy
entries.definitionCN: 懒惰的

normalIntro.en: Industrious is the old Latin effort sense of industry, worn as an adjective.
normalIntro.cn: industrious 是 industry 里那层古老的拉丁「努力」义，披着形容词外衣。

normal.en: Industrious is an adjective, not a verb: it describes a person, not a factory.
normal.cn: industrious 是形容词，不是动词：它描述人，不描述工厂。

normal.en: The adverb is industriously, and the noun is industriousness.
normal.cn: 副词是 industriously，名词是 industriousness。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with industrial, which is about factories and trade.
normal.cn: 别和 industrial 混淆，那个词说的是工厂和产业。

normal.en: Industrious goes with people, ants, and bees, all busy with steady work.
normal.cn: industrious 常与「人」「蚂蚁」「蜜蜂」搭配，都忙个不停。

normal.en: The Latin root industria means effort, so an industrious person is full of it.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 industria 意为努力，所以 industrious 的人身上满是这股劲。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp still burning on a desk at midnight.
abstract.cn: 想象凌晨还亮着灯的写字台。

abstract.en: Imagine hands that are always holding tools or a pen.
abstract.cn: 想象一双手总攥着工具或笔。

abstract.en: Think of a beehive where no bee ever sits still.
abstract.cn: 想象一个没有一只蜜蜂闲着的蜂巢。

examples.en: He was an industrious farmer who rarely rested.
examples.cn: 他是个很少休息的勤劳农夫。

examples.en: Industrious bees pollinate the orchard every spring.
examples.cn: 勤劳的蜜蜂每年春天为果园授粉。

examples.en: Her industrious habits led to a place at university.
examples.cn: 她勤奋的习惯让她考上了大学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因打石头咧，饿斯」——为了打石头挣口饭吃，天天干活，饿着也干，就是勤劳；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 industria（勤奋、努力）→ 拉丁语 industrius（勤勉的）→ 英语 industrious（勤劳的）；与 industry（工业）同出一源，但 industrious 保留了最早的「努力」义，而 industry 后来更多指向「工业」。

sensesIntro.en: Industrious always describes steady effort: at everyday work, then at study, then in a playful way for busy animals, and finally as a slightly formal word of praise.
sensesIntro.cn: industrious 始终描述踏实的努力：先是日常劳作，再是学习用功，接着带点趣味地形容忙碌的动物，最后是一句略带正式的赞语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worker up before sunrise, hands never still.
core.cn: 核心意象：天没亮就起身干活、手一直不闲的人。

branches.en: Steady everyday work is the core adjective sense.
branches.cn: 日常劳作中的踏实卖力，是核心的形容词义。

branches.en: Applying the same effort to learning gives the study sense.
branches.cn: 把同样的努力用到学习上，就是学习用功的义项。

branches.en: Borrowing the word for busy animals keeps the idea of constant activity.
branches.cn: 把这个词借给忙碌的动物，保留的是不停活动的意味。

branches.en: The formal tone comes from the Latin origin and makes the word a careful compliment.
branches.cn: 正式的语气来自拉丁语出身，使这个词成了一句慎重的称赞。

branches.en: A hard worker and an eager student share the same quiet persistence.
branches.cn: 勤劳的劳动者与用功的学生共享同一种安静的坚持。

intro.en: Industrious keeps an old Latin adjective ending, while its modern relatives grew from the industry noun.
intro.cn: industrious 保留了古老的拉丁形容词词尾，而它的现代同族词大多由 industry 名词长出。

latinIntro.en: Latin industria means effort, and its adjective industrius means diligent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 industria 意为努力，其形容词 industrius 意为勤勉的。

items.example: Industria is the noun behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: industria 是整个词族背后的名词。

items.example: Industrius is the direct ancestor of industrious.
items.exampleCN: industrius 是 industrious 的直接来源。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ous gives the adjective its ending.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 提供形容词的结尾。

items.example: Industrious is the adjective form.
items.exampleCN: industrious 是形容词形式。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms industriously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 industriously。

items.example: They worked industriously all night.
items.exampleCN: 他们整夜勤勉地工作。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms industriousness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 industriousness。

items.example: Industriousness earned him a promotion.
items.exampleCN: 勤勉让他升了职。

items.example: Industry shares the Latin root.
items.exampleCN: industry 共享同一拉丁词根。

items.example: Industrialise looks close but points at factories.
items.exampleCN: industrialise 看起来相近，但指向工厂。

definition_zh: 不能吃的；不适合食用的；难以下咽的
definition_en: not fit to be eaten, either because it is harmful or because it is too unpleasant to swallow
core_image: 盘子里那块发霉的面包，被推到一边没人动
scene: 冰箱深处那盒过期的酱已经长毛了。That jar of sauce has gone mouldy and is now completely inedible.
sceneCN: 这里 inedible 是「不能吃的、不宜食用的」（第 1 个义项：因变质或有害而不可入口）；句意：那罐酱已经发霉，现在完全不能吃了。

pos.zh: 不能吃的；不宜食用的；难以下咽的

derivatives.zh: 去前缀后的肯定形式，义为「可食用的」
由 inedible 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「不可食用的性质」
由 inedible 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「无法食用地」

senses.title: Not safe to eat
senses.definition: too harmful, spoiled, or dirty to be eaten safely
senses.definitionCN: 因有害、变质或不洁而无法安全食用
senses.example: The meat had gone bad and was inedible.
senses.exampleCN: 这肉已经坏了，不能吃了。
senses.why: The prefix in- means not, and edibilis means fit to eat, so inedible simply means not fit to eat.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 表示「不」，edibilis 意为「可食用的」，所以 inedible 就是「不适合吃」。

senses.title: Not eaten by people
senses.definition: of a plant, fungus, or other creature, never eaten by people, though not always poisonous
senses.definitionCN: 指某种植物、菌类或其他生物从不被人食用，但未必有毒
senses.example: Many inedible mushrooms grow under the pine trees.
senses.exampleCN: 松树下长着许多不可食用的蘑菇。
senses.why: Field guides borrow the word for species that are simply outside human food, where the line is custom rather than danger.
senses.whyCN: 野外图鉴把这个词用于根本不在人类食谱里的物种，此时界线来自习惯，而不是危险。

senses.title: Too awful to swallow
senses.definition: perfectly harmless but so badly made or bitter that nobody wants to eat it
senses.definitionCN: 本来无害，却因难吃或苦涩而没人愿意吃
senses.example: My first attempt at soup was thin and inedible.
senses.exampleCN: 我头一回煮的汤又稀又难以下咽。
senses.why: If fit for eating is the test, something cooked so badly that it cannot be eaten fails the same test for taste.
senses.whyCN: 既然标准是「适不适合吃」，那么做得差到吃不下去的东西，同样通不过这道口味上的关。

senses.title: Used for things that are not food
senses.definition: used of paper, plastic, or other objects that people try to eat by mistake
senses.definitionCN: 指纸、塑料等可能被人误食的物件
senses.example: Keep small inedible parts away from toddlers.
senses.exampleCN: 把细小、不能吃的零件放在幼儿够不到的地方。
senses.why: Once the word names anything unfit for the mouth, it can describe objects a child might put in it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指任何不适合入口的东西，它就能用来描述小孩可能塞进嘴里的物件。

intro.en: Inedible joins the negative prefix in- to edible, which comes from Latin edere, to eat.
intro.cn: inedible 由否定前缀 in- 与 edible 组成，而 edible 来自拉丁语 edere（吃）。

items.en: Edere means to eat, giving the past participle esus, eaten.
items.cn: edere 意为吃，其过去分词 esus 意为「被吃掉的」。

items.en: Late scientific Latin forms edibilis, fit to eat.
items.cn: 晚期的科学拉丁语构成 edibilis，意为「适合吃的」。

items.en: Edible enters English meaning fit to be eaten.
items.cn: edible 进入英语，意为可食用的。

items.en: The Latin prefix in- is added to make inedible, and the first recorded uses are often in the negative.
items.cn: 加上拉丁否定前缀 in- 构成 inedible，早期记录多出现在否定语境中。

items.en: Modern use extends from spoiled food to foods, plants, and objects that must not be eaten.
items.cn: 现代用法从变质食物，扩展到不宜食用的食品、植物乃至物件。

note.en: Inedible is the negative of edible; its look-alikes share the in- prefix, and its near meanings describe who may eat what.
note.cn: inedible 是 edible 的否定形式；形近词共享 in- 前缀，近义词则描述谁可以吃什么。

entries.definitionCN: 可食用的
难以置信的；同用 in- 前缀，词干不同
失去知觉的；未察觉的；只是拼写相近，词源不同
不好吃的；难以下咽的

entries.definition: so badly cooked that it is hard to eat
entries.definitionCN: 难以下口；多指烹饪失败

entries.definition: likely to kill or harm if eaten or touched
entries.definitionCN: 有毒的

normalIntro.en: Inedible is edible with a Latin no in front of it: not fit to eat.
normalIntro.cn: inedible 就是在 edible 前面加一个拉丁语的「不」：不适合吃。

normal.en: The prefix in- means not, as in invisible and incredible.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 表示不，如 invisible、incredible 都是这样。

normal.en: The stem edible comes from Latin edere, to eat.
normal.cn: 词干 edible 来自拉丁语 edere（吃）。

normal.en: Inedible usually pairs with food, plants, or parts, and often with the phrase do not eat.
normal.cn: inedible 常与食物、植物、零件搭配，常和「不要吃」这类说法同现。

normal.en: Keep the contrast: edible means you may eat it, unpalatable means it tastes bad.
normal.cn: 记住对比：edible 指可以吃，unpalatable 指味道不好。

normal.en: Inedible is the standard negative of edible, while uneatable is mostly spoken and about failed cooking.
normal.cn: inedible 是 edible 的规范否定形式，而 uneatable 多为口语，指做菜失败。

abstract.en: Picture a plate pushed away with a hand raised in refusal.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘菜被推开，一只手抬起来表示拒绝。

abstract.en: Imagine a jar of jam turned green and hairy.
abstract.cn: 想象一罐果酱变得发绿、长满长毛。

abstract.en: Think of a mushroom sign with a fork and a red line through it.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚蘑菇旁边画着叉子的标志，上面一道红线横过。

examples.en: Some berries in this forest are inedible.
examples.cn: 这片林子里有些浆果不能吃。

examples.en: The bread had gone inedible after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后面包变得没法吃了。

examples.en: The recipe was ruined, leaving an inedible mess.
examples.cn: 配方弄砸了，留下一锅难以下咽的东西。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因得赔了」——吃了这东西得赔钱治病，可见它是不能吃的；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 edere（吃）→ 分词 esus（已吃的）→ 晚期拉丁 edibilis（可食的）→ 英语 edible（可食用的）→ 加否定前缀 in- 构成 inedible（不可食用的）；核心是「放进嘴里」与「进不了嘴」的对立。

sensesIntro.en: Inedible starts with food that is unsafe to eat, then covers edible-by-custom plants, then food ruined by bad cooking, and finally non-food things that must stay out of the mouth.
sensesIntro.cn: inedible 先从不能安全食用的食物讲起，再扩大到按习惯不吃的植物，然后是做坏了难以下咽的食物，最后是必须远离口腔的非食物物件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mouldy loaf pushed to the edge of the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：发霉的面包被推到桌边。

branches.en: Spoiled or dangerous food is the most common sense.
branches.cn: 变质或有害的食物，是最常见的义项。

branches.en: Plants outside human custom carry the same label in field guides.
branches.cn: 野外图鉴里，按习惯不吃的植物也用同一个标签。

branches.en: Bad cooking fails the taste test, so it joins the same word.
branches.cn: 烹饪失败过不了口味这一关，于是也归进这个词。

branches.en: Objects that must not be swallowed stretch the word beyond food.
branches.cn: 不该被吞下的物件，把这个词从食物扩展到非食物。

branches.en: Danger and bad taste both end in a refusal at the table.
branches.cn: 危险与难吃，最终都落在餐桌上的拒绝。

intro.en: Inedible is a Latin negative prefix on a Latin eating stem, with English -able as the bridge.
intro.cn: inedible 是拉丁否定前缀加拉丁语「吃」词干，再以英语词尾 -able 连接而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin edere means to eat, and -ible marks something that can be done.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 edere 意为吃，-ible 表示「可以被……」的意思。

items.example: Edere carries the act of eating.
items.exampleCN: edere 承载「吃」这个动作。

items.example: Esus is the past participle of edere.
items.exampleCN: esus 是 edere 的过去分词。

items.example: Edibilis pairs the stem with the -ibilis ending.
items.exampleCN: edibilis 把词干与 -ibilis 词尾拼在一起。

items.example: The suffix -ible forms edible.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ible 构成 edible。

items.example: Edible is the positive partner.
items.exampleCN: edible 是肯定形式。

items.example: The prefix in- reverses edible.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把 edible 反过来。

items.example: Inedible is the negative form.
items.exampleCN: inedible 是否定形式。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms inedibility.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 inedibility。

items.example: Inedibleness is a rarer variant of the noun.
items.exampleCN: inedibleness 是较少见的名词变体。

items.meaning: too hard or bad to eat
items.example: Uneatable uses the English un- instead.
items.exampleCN: uneatable 改用英语前缀 un-。

definition_zh: 效率低的；不经济的；浪费的；能力差的
definition_en: not achieving the best possible result with the time, money, or effort that is used
core_image: 一台漏水的管道：水一路滴到地上，真正流进桶里的只剩一半
scene: 车间的旧机器又吵又慢，同样的时间只产出别人的一半。The old machines in the workshop are noisy and slow, so the whole line is inefficient.
sceneCN: 这里 inefficient 是「效率低的」（第 1 个义项：做事方式费时费力却不划算）；句意：车间的旧机器又吵又慢，整条生产线效率低下。

pos.zh: 效率低的；不经济的；浪费的
能力差的；不称职的

derivatives.zh: inefficient 去 -t 加名词后缀 -cy 构成，义为「低效、浪费」
inefficient 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「低效地」
去掉否定前缀 in- 后的肯定形式，义为「高效的」（反义词）
efficient 的肯定名词形式，义为「效率」

senses.title: Using time and money badly
senses.definition: not producing good results in relation to the time, money, or effort that is spent
senses.definitionCN: 与所花的时间、金钱或精力相比，没有产出好的结果
senses.example: Calling a separate meeting for every decision proved inefficient.
senses.exampleCN: 每个决定都单独开一次会，事实证明这样效率很低。
senses.why: Inefficient is efficient with the negative prefix in-, so the core is a process that does not reach its purpose at full speed.
senses.whyCN: inefficient 就是 efficient 加上否定前缀 in-，核心是一个没能全速抵达目的的过程，所以先指做事的「效率低」。

senses.title: Wasting resources
senses.definition: using more fuel, water, material, or energy than is needed for a job
senses.definitionCN: 为完成一项工作而使用了超出需要的燃料、水、材料或能源
senses.example: Old boilers are inefficient and burn far too much gas.
senses.exampleCN: 旧锅炉效率很低，燃气消耗远远过量。
senses.why: When a process misses its purpose, the extra time and fuel have to go somewhere, so the image shifts from lost speed to wasted material.
senses.whyCN: 过程偏离目的时，多花的时间和燃料总要有去处，于是意象从「慢」滑向「浪费」，义项便从效率低长成浪费资源。

senses.title: Bad at a job
senses.definition: not able to do a job well, so that others have to correct the work
senses.definitionCN: 不能把工作做好，以致别人不得不来弥补或返工
senses.example: The new office manager is well liked but inefficient.
senses.exampleCN: 新来的办公室主管人缘很好，但办事能力差。
senses.why: If the tool is the person, an inefficient worker is simply a device that turns effort into little output.
senses.whyCN: 若把工具换成人，inefficient 就形容一个人费力多、成果少，于是引申出「能力差、不称职」。

senses.title: Badly organised market
senses.definition: in economics, describing a market that does not use resources in the way that gives the most benefit
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中形容市场未能以产生最大收益的方式使用资源
senses.example: Price controls can make a market inefficient and create shortages.
senses.exampleCN: 价格管制可能让市场配置低效并造成短缺。
senses.why: Economics turns the wasteful process into a technical label for a system that wastes its resources.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把「浪费的过程」升级为术语，专指浪费资源的市场，这是义项二的延伸用法。

intro.en: Inefficient is the Latin prefix in- meaning not, joined to efficient, from efficere, to accomplish.
intro.cn: inefficient 是拉丁语前缀 in-（不）加 efficient（有效率的）构成，而 efficient 源于拉丁语 efficere（完成）。

items.en: Efficere combines ex, out, with facere, to do, and means to carry out or accomplish.
items.cn: efficere 由 ex（出来）与 facere（做）合成，意为执行、完成。

items.en: Efficiens is the present participle, meaning doing or achieving.
items.cn: efficiens 是现在分词，意为「在做的、能达成的」。

items.en: Scholastic writers, especially in philosophy, make efficiens a technical word for a cause that produces an effect.
items.cn: 经院哲学的作者把 efficiens 变成术语，指产生效果的「原因」。

items.en: English borrows the word from Old French, where it is attested in the same period.
items.cn: 英语经古法语借入该词，同一时期古法语中已有记载。

items.en: The prefix in- is added and inefficient comes to mean not producing the intended result.
items.cn: 加上否定前缀 in- 后，inefficient 表示「未产生预期结果的」。

items.en: In industry and economics the word settles on wasting effort, time, or fuel.
items.cn: 在工业与经济语境中，这个词固定为「浪费精力、时间或燃料」。

note.en: Inefficient sits with efficient and effect, and near wasteful and ineffective.
note.cn: inefficient 与 efficient、effect 同族，与 wasteful、ineffective 意义相近。

entries.definitionCN: 去掉 in- 的肯定形式，义为高效的

entries.definition: a state of wasting time or money
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，义为低效、浪费
同样是 in- 加效字根的同族词，但侧重完全没有效果，而非费力太多

entries.definition: using more of something than is necessary
entries.definitionCN: 浪费的，比 inefficient 更强调消耗本身多
不经济的，侧重花钱与资源

entries.definition: producing a good amount of something
entries.definitionCN: 反义对照：高产的

normalIntro.en: Inefficient is in- plus effect: a process that does not get to its effect.
normalIntro.cn: inefficient 是 in- 加 effect：一个走不到「效果」的过程。

normal.en: In- negates and ficere is to make, so inefficient makes little out of much.
normal.cn: in- 表否定，ficere 表制作，所以 inefficient 是投入很多、产出很少。

normal.en: The noun is inefficiency, the adverb is inefficiently.
normal.cn: 名词是 inefficiency，副词是 inefficiently。

normal.en: Its direct opposite is efficient, a single letter away.
normal.cn: 它的直接反义词是 efficient，只差开头一个否定前缀。

normal.en: Inefficient use of resources is a standard collocation.
normal.cn: inefficient use of resources 是标准搭配。

normal.en: Keep it apart from ineffective, which means no result at all.
normal.cn: 要区别于 ineffective：那个是完全没有效果。

abstract.en: Picture a pail with a hole, so half the water never arrives.
abstract.cn: 第一组画面：木桶底有个洞，水半路就漏光了。

abstract.en: Imagine a car burning fuel only to sit in traffic.
abstract.cn: 第二组画面：汽车烧着油，却困在车流里动弹不得。

abstract.en: See a clerk shuffling the same paper six times.
abstract.cn: 第三组画面：职员把同一张纸反复倒腾了六遍。

examples.en: The firm was criticised for its inefficient use of public money.
examples.cn: 这家公司因低效使用公共资金而受到批评。

examples.en: It is inefficient to print every draft when you can read it on screen.
examples.cn: 稿子能在屏幕上看，却偏要打印每一稿，这很低效。

examples.en: The chief engineer wrote a report blaming inefficient management for the delay.
examples.cn: 总工程师写了一份报告，把延误归咎于低效的管理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因非・费神」——因方法不对而白白费神，就是「效率低」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ efficere（完成、做成，由 ex 出 + facere 做）→ efficiens（能达成的）→ efficient（有效的）→ inefficient（无效的；低效的），核心义「做不到应有效果」。

sensesIntro.en: Inefficient moves from doing a job with wasted time and money, to wasting resources, to a person who does not do a job well, and finally to an economic term.
sensesIntro.cn: inefficient 从「做事费时费钱」出发，扩到「浪费资源」，再形容「能力差的人」，最后成为描述市场配置的术语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pipe that leaks, so only part of the water reaches the bucket.
core.cn: 核心意象：漏水的管道，只有一部分水真的流进桶里。

branches.en: Spending much to get little is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 投入多产出少，是日常义项。

branches.en: Equipment that burns too much is the resource side of the same image.
branches.cn: 设备耗能过多，是同一意象的资源面。

branches.en: The image applied to a person becomes lack of ability.
branches.cn: 同一意象用在人身上，就成了能力不足。

branches.en: Both senses describe a process that keeps losing what it takes in.
branches.cn: 两个义项都描述一个不断流失输入的过程。

branches.en: In economics, wasted resources in a market are named with the same leak.
branches.cn: 在经济学里，市场的资源流失也用这个「漏水」来命名。

intro.en: Inefficient is built from the negative prefix in- and the facere family, alongside efficient, effect, and efficient use.
intro.cn: inefficient 由否定前缀 in- 与 facere 一族构成，同族有 efficient、effect 和常见搭配 efficient use。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- means not, and efficere means to accomplish, giving the idea of something that fails to reach its goal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in- 表示「不」，efficere 表示「完成」，合起来就是「达不到目标」。

items.example: The prefix in- turns efficient into its opposite.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把 efficient 变成它的反义。

items.example: Facere is the base of effect and factory.
items.exampleCN: facere 是 effect、factory 的共同基础。

items.example: Efficere combines ex and facere.
items.exampleCN: efficere 由 ex 与 facere 合成。

items.example: Efficient is the base word.
items.exampleCN: efficient 是基础词。

items.example: Inefficient adds the negative prefix.
items.exampleCN: inefficient 加上了否定前缀。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms inefficiently.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 inefficiently。

items.example: The suffix -cy forms inefficiency.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -cy 构成 inefficiency。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms effective and ineffective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成 effective 与 ineffective。

items.example: Ineffective is a sister word in the same family.
items.exampleCN: ineffective 是同族的姊妹词。

definition_zh: 不合格的；无资格的；不符合条件的；不宜婚配的
definition_en: not allowed to do something or to receive something, because you do not meet the rules or conditions
core_image: 报名窗口前被退回表格：表格上盖着一枚红色章，章上写着「条件不符」
scene: 球队多报了一名外援，联赛注册处审核后把名单退回了。The club has one foreign player too many, so the league has declared him ineligible.
sceneCN: 这里 ineligible 是「无参赛资格的」（第 3 个义项：不符合某项规则或条件）；句意：球队多报了一名外援，联赛宣布他无参赛资格。

pos.zh: 不合格的；无资格的；不符合条件的
不宜婚配的

derivatives.zh: ineligible 去 -le 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「不合格、无资格」
ineligible 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，书面表示「以不合格的方式」
去掉否定前缀 in- 后的肯定形式，义为「合格的；有资格的」
eligible 的肯定名词形式，义为「资格、合格条件」

senses.title: Not allowed by the rules
senses.definition: not permitted to take part in something or to receive something because the rules exclude you
senses.definitionCN: 因不符合规则而不被允许参加某事或获得某物
senses.example: Employees under twenty are ineligible for the bonus.
senses.exampleCN: 二十岁以下的员工没有资格领取奖金。
senses.why: Ineligible is eligible with in-, and the Latin eligere meant to choose out, so the core is being left out of the chosen group.
senses.whyCN: ineligible 就是 eligible 加否定前缀 in-，而拉丁语 eligere 本义是「挑出来」，所以核心是「没被挑进名单」。

senses.title: Short of a condition
senses.titleCN: 不符合条件的；不适任的
senses.definition: not meeting a stated requirement such as experience, documents, or status
senses.definitionCN: 不满足明确写出的要求，如经验、材料或身份条件
senses.example: The application was rejected because the candidate was ineligible on experience.
senses.exampleCN: 申请被拒，因为该候选人在经验条件上不合格。
senses.why: Choosing out a person happens for a stated reason, so the word grows to name the missing condition itself.
senses.whyCN: 把人从名单中挑除总要有理由，于是这个词顺势指「缺了某个条件」。

senses.title: Ruled out in sport
senses.definition: in sport, not allowed to play because of the rules, a contract, or a ban
senses.definitionCN: 体育中因规则、合同或禁赛而不被允许上场
senses.example: He was ruled ineligible for the final after a red card.
senses.exampleCN: 他因红牌被判定无决赛参赛资格。
senses.why: League rules work like a list of chosen players, and the umpire strikes a name off it.
senses.whyCN: 联赛规则就像一份选中的球员名单，裁判把名字划掉，这个词就有了赛场义。

senses.title: Not fit to marry
senses.definition: old formal use: not a suitable partner for marriage because of social position or conduct
senses.definitionCN: 旧时正式用法：因地位或品行而不适合作为婚配对象
senses.example: In older novels a poor tutor is often called ineligible.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧小说里，清贫的家庭教师常被说成「不配结婚」。
senses.why: Marriage once counted as an office you were chosen for, so an unsuitable partner became ineligible.
senses.whyCN: 旧时婚姻被看作一种「被选中的身份」，条件不够的对象自然被说成 ineligible，于是生出这个特殊义项。

intro.en: Ineligible is the Latin prefix in- meaning not, added to eligible, from eligere, to choose out.
intro.cn: ineligible 是拉丁语前缀 in-（不）加 eligible（有资格的）构成，而 eligible 源于 eligere（挑出）。

items.en: Eligere combines ex, out, with legere, to gather or pick, and means to pick out.
items.cn: eligere 由 ex（出来）与 legere（拾取）合成，意为「挑出、选出」。

items.en: Eligibilis is a later church and legal adjective meaning that may be chosen.
items.cn: eligibilis 是较晚的中世纪形容词，多用于教会与法律文本，意为「可以当选的」。

items.en: Eligible passes from Latin into French and is used for those fit to be chosen.
items.cn: eligible 由拉丁语进入法语，指「适合被选中的」。

items.en: English takes eligible for the person who may be chosen, and ineligible appears as its negative.
items.cn: 英语借入 eligible，指「可以被选中的人」，ineligible 随即作为它的否定形式出现。

items.en: The word spreads to examinations and offices, meaning wanting in the required qualifications.
items.cn: 该词扩用到考试与职位，表示「缺少所需资格」。

items.en: Now it covers benefits, sport bans, and visas, with the idea of being struck off a list.
items.cn: 如今用于福利、禁赛与签证，都保留「被从名单上划掉」的意味。

note.en: Ineligible shares the legere picking family with eligible and elect, and is close to unqualified and disqualified.
note.cn: ineligible 与 eligible、elect 共享「挑选」词根，意义靠近 unqualified、disqualified。

entries.definition: allowed to do or receive something
entries.definitionCN: 去掉 in- 的肯定形式，义为有资格的

entries.definition: the state of not being allowed
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，义为无资格的状态
拼写只差一个字母，意为无法辨认的，与 ineligible 的词源无关

entries.definition: lacking the training or right to do something
entries.definitionCN: 侧重缺少资历或技能

entries.definition: legally barred after breaking a rule
entries.definitionCN: 强调因违规被取消资格，往往已发生
反义对照：有资格的

normalIntro.en: Ineligible is in- plus eligere: you are not chosen out of the list.
normalIntro.cn: ineligible 是 in- 加 eligere：你没有被从名单里挑出来。

normal.en: The legere root behind eligible also gives select and elect.
normal.cn: eligible 背后的 legere 词根也造出了 select 和 elect。

normal.en: The noun is ineligibility, the adverb is ineligibly.
normal.cn: 名词是 ineligibility，副词是 ineligibly。

normal.en: Inelegible only looks alike but means unreadable.
normal.cn: inelegible 只是形似，意思是难以辨认的。

normal.en: Ineligible for is the most common pattern.
normal.cn: 最常见的是 ineligible for 这个搭配。

normal.en: Disqualified is what happens after a breach, ineligible is what the rules say in advance.
normal.cn: disqualified 是违规后被取消，ineligible 是规则一开始就不允许。

abstract.en: Picture a list of chosen names with your own crossed out.
abstract.cn: 第一组画面：入选名单上一个名字被划掉，正是你自己。

abstract.en: See a form returned with a red stamp: conditions not met.
abstract.cn: 第二组画面：表格被退回，上面盖着红章「条件不符」。

abstract.en: Hear the stadium announcer saying this player cannot take the field.
abstract.cn: 第三组画面：球场广播宣布这名球员不能上场。

examples.en: Students who started the course after the deadline are ineligible for the refund.
examples.cn: 截止日期之后才开课的学生没有退款资格。

examples.en: The team was found to have fielded an ineligible player in the cup match.
examples.cn: 该队伍被发现让一名无资格的球员参加了杯赛。

examples.en: Because he holds dual citizenship, he was declared ineligible for the diplomatic post.
examples.cn: 由于持有双重国籍，他被认定不具备担任该外交职位的资格。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因累鸡脖」——因为太累，脖子都扛不住，被考官判定「不合格」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ eligere（挑出，由 ex 出 + legere 拾取）→ eligibilis（可被选中的）→ 英语 eligible（有资格的）→ ineligible（无资格的），核心义「未被选入名单」。

sensesIntro.en: Ineligible starts as a person kept off a list by the rules, broadens to missing a condition, then covers sport bans and old marriage talk.
sensesIntro.cn: ineligible 先指被规则挡在名单外的人，再泛化为缺少条件，之后用于体育禁赛，最后保留一个旧时的婚配义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name struck off the list of chosen people.
core.cn: 核心意象：入选名单上的名字被划掉。

branches.en: Being kept off the list is the central sense.
branches.cn: 被挡在名单外是核心义项。

branches.en: A named condition that is not met explains why the name went.
branches.cn: 某个条件没满足，解释了名字为何被划掉。

branches.en: Sport rules keep an athlete off the team sheet in the same way.
branches.cn: 体育规则以同样的方式把运动员挡在出场名单之外。

branches.en: Both describe the formal reason for being refused.
branches.cn: 两者都描述被拒绝的正式理由。

branches.en: Old marriage talk borrowed the same choosing image for partners.
branches.cn: 旧时的婚配说法同样是借「挑人」的意象。

intro.en: Ineligible offers the negative prefix in-, the legere choosing root, and family words such as elect and select.
intro.cn: ineligible 给出否定前缀 in- 与 legere「挑选」词根，同族词包括 elect、select。

latinIntro.en: Latin eligere means to pick out, built from ex and legere, to gather or choose.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 eligere 意为挑出，由 ex 与 legere（拾取、选择）构成。

items.example: The prefix in- makes eligible negative.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把 eligible 变成否定。

items.example: Ex- adds the idea of picking out.
items.exampleCN: ex- 加了「挑出来」的方向。

items.meaning: to gather, to pick, to read
items.example: Legere gives lect and legend.
items.exampleCN: legere 也造出 lect 与 legend。

items.example: Eligere is the direct root of eligible.
items.exampleCN: eligere 是 eligible 的直接词根。

items.example: Eligible is the base word.
items.exampleCN: eligible 是基础词。

items.example: Ineligible adds the negative prefix.
items.exampleCN: ineligible 加上否定前缀。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms ineligibility.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 ineligibility。

items.example: Elect keeps the choosing sense.
items.exampleCN: elect 保留「选择」义。

items.example: Select shares the same Latin root.
items.exampleCN: select 共享同一拉丁词根。

definition_zh: 笨拙的；不称职的；无能的；不恰当的
definition_en: having no skill at something, or showing a clumsy lack of skill
core_image: 笨手笨脚的新手握着螺丝刀，把好端端的螺丝拧花了
scene: 新来的实习生拆了半天打印机，装回去时多出三颗螺丝。The new intern spent half a day stripping the printer and rebuilt it with three screws left over, an inept job from start to finish.
sceneCN: 这里 inept 是「笨拙的、不熟练的」（第 1 个义项：缺少做事所需的手艺）；句意：新来的实习生拆了半天打印机，装回去时多出三颗螺丝，从头到尾都做得笨手笨脚。

pos.zh: 笨拙的；不称职的；无能的
不恰当的；不得体的

collocations.phrase: an inept handling of the situation

derivatives.zh: inept 加名词后缀 -itude 构成，义为「无能、笨拙」
inept 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「笨拙地」
inept 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「笨拙、不得体」
去掉否定前缀 in- 的肯定形式，义为「熟练的」

senses.title: Clumsy with the hands
senses.definition: having little skill at doing something with your hands, so the work is clumsy
senses.definitionCN: 手上缺少做某事的本领，做出来的活儿显得笨拙
senses.example: Holding a needle makes me feel completely inept.
senses.exampleCN: 一拿针我就觉得自己笨手笨脚。
senses.why: Inept is in- plus apt, and apt meant fitted to a job, so inept is the hand that does not fit the tool.
senses.whyCN: inept 是 in- 加 apt，而 apt 本义是「配上、合手」，所以 inept 就是「不合手、不会用工具」。

senses.title: Not fit for the post
senses.definition: lacking the ability or judgement that a job or role demands
senses.definitionCN: 缺少某项工作或职位所要求的能力或判断力
senses.example: The committee called the minister inept after the failed rescue.
senses.exampleCN: 救援失败后，委员会称这位部长无能。
senses.why: An apt official is fitted to the office, so the same image turns into official duty that the person cannot match.
senses.whyCN: apt 的官员是「与岗位相配」的人，同一意象一转就成了「与职责不相配」，于是指不称职。

senses.title: Clumsy with words and people
senses.titleCN: 不擅交际的；笨嘴拙舌的
senses.definition: awkward in social situations or careless in what you say to others
senses.definitionCN: 在社交场合显得局促，或说话时不顾及他人感受
senses.example: His inept joke about the boss silenced the whole room.
senses.exampleCN: 他那个拿老板开玩笑的拙劣笑话让全场安静下来。
senses.why: Apt also named fit words in rhetoric, so inept speech is wording that does not fit the moment.
senses.whyCN: apt 在修辞里也指「贴切的话」，所以 inept speech 就是不合场合、不贴切的言辞。

senses.title: Out of place
senses.definition: formal use: not suitable for the occasion or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 正式用法：与场合或目的不相称
senses.example: It seemed inept to celebrate while the flood victims were homeless.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水灾民无家可归时还办庆祝活动，显得很不恰当。
senses.why: When the people and the words are set aside, only the fit remains, so inept can describe the thing that does not belong.
senses.whyCN: 把人、话都放到一边，只剩「是否合适」这一层，于是 inept 也能形容不合时宜的事物。

intro.en: Inept comes from Latin ineptus, meaning not apt or not fitting, which is in-, not, plus aptus, fitted.
intro.cn: inept 来自拉丁语 ineptus（不合宜的），即 in-（不）加 aptus（相配的）。

items.en: The reconstructed root ap- carries the idea of to fit, to reach, and is shared with Latin aptus.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 ap- 含有「相配、接触」之义，与拉丁语 aptus 同源（重构形式）。

items.en: Aptus means fitted or suited, from the verb apisci, to reach or obtain.
items.cn: aptus 意为相配的、适宜的，来自动词 apisci（触及、获得）。

items.en: Ineptus describes a person or thing that is out of place or unsuited.
items.cn: ineptus 形容人物或事物不合时宜、不相配。

items.en: The word reaches French as inepte, still with the sense of unfitting.
items.cn: 该词以 inepte 进入法语，仍保留「不合宜」之义。

items.en: English adopts inept and shifts it towards lack of skill and ability.
items.cn: 英语借入 inept，并转向「缺乏技巧与能力」。

items.en: Today inept is used for clumsy hands, bad officials, and awkward remarks.
items.cn: 今天 inept 可形容笨手、庸官和不妥的话。

note.en: Inept is the negative of apt, close to ineptitude and ineptly, and near clumsy and incompetent.
note.cn: inept 是 apt 的否定形式，同族有 ineptitude、ineptly，意义接近 clumsy、incompetent。

entries.definitionCN: 去掉 in- 的肯定形式，义为恰当的、聪敏的
派生名词，义为无能、笨拙
拼写与 inept 只差一个字母，同源，侧重「不合适」而非「不熟练」
笨手笨脚的，最口语的说法

entries.definition: not having the ability to do a job
entries.definitionCN: 不称职的，比 inept 更正式
尴尬的、不自在的

normalIntro.en: Inept is in- plus apt: the thing that does not fit the hand, the job, or the moment.
normalIntro.cn: inept 是 in- 加 apt：不合手、不称职、不合时宜。

normal.en: Apt comes from Latin aptus, fitted, so inept is not fitted.
normal.cn: apt 源于拉丁语 aptus（相配的），所以 inept 是「配不上」。

normal.en: The noun ineptitude is strong and formal.
normal.cn: 名词 ineptitude 语气强、偏正式。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with inapt, which means unsuitable.
normal.cn: 不要和 inapt 混淆，那个是「不合适」。

normal.en: Socially inept is common for a person who talks badly with others.
normal.cn: socially inept 常用来形容不擅交际的人。

normal.en: Adapt carries the same apt, meaning made to fit.
normal.cn: adapt 也含 apt，表示「使之相配」。

abstract.en: See a screwdriver handle far too wide for a small hand.
abstract.cn: 第一组画面：螺丝刀柄太粗，小手怎么也握不稳。

abstract.en: Imagine a minister reading the wrong page at the podium.
abstract.cn: 第二组画面：部长在台上念错了那一页。

abstract.en: Hear a joke land in total silence at a party.
abstract.cn: 第三组画面：聚会上一个笑话落地，全场鸦雀无声。

examples.en: He was famously inept at small talk and usually left parties early.
examples.cn: 他出了名地不擅长闲聊，常常提前离开聚会。

examples.en: The council was blamed for its inept handling of the housing crisis.
examples.cn: 市议会因对住房危机的处理拙劣而受到指责。

examples.en: Her first attempt at baking was inept, but the cake still tasted fine.
examples.cn: 她第一次烘焙做得很笨拙，不过蛋糕味道还不错。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一捏破」——手艺太差，一捏就把东西捏破了，正是「笨拙」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ aptus（相配的、合宜的，源自 apisci 触及、获得）→ ineptus（不合宜的）→ 法语 inepte → 英语 inept，核心义「配不上」。

sensesIntro.en: Inept runs from hands that cannot use a tool, to a person unfit for an office, to awkward speech, and finally to anything out of place.
sensesIntro.cn: inept 从「手不合工具」出发，扩到「人不合职位」，再到「话不合场合」，最后泛指任何不合宜的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that does not fit the tool it must hold.
core.cn: 核心意象：握工具的手与工具配不上。

branches.en: The hand that does not fit the tool is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 手与工具不相配，是字面义项。

branches.en: A person who does not fit an office is called inept.
branches.cn: 人配不上职位，就叫不称职。

branches.en: Words that do not fit the people around create social clumsiness.
branches.cn: 言语配不上身边的人，就造成社交上的笨拙。

branches.en: Both senses judge whether skill matches the task.
branches.cn: 两者都在判断能力是否与任务相配。

branches.en: When fit is judged by the occasion alone, we get the general sense of unsuitable.
branches.cn: 只看场合是否相合，就得到泛指的「不恰当」义项。

intro.en: Inept joins the negative prefix in- to apt, in the family of adapt and aptitude, all built on the sense of fitting.
intro.cn: inept 把否定前缀 in- 与 apt 结合，同族有 adapt、aptitude，都以「相配」为核心。

latinIntro.en: Latin aptus means fitted or suited, from apisci, to reach, so in- marks what never fits.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aptus 意为相配的，来自 apisci（触及），加 in- 就表示「配不上」。

items.example: The prefix in- negates apt.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把 apt 否定。

items.example: Aptus comes from apisci, to reach.
items.exampleCN: aptus 来自 apisci（触及）。

items.example: Ineptus is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: ineptus 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Apt is the positive stem.
items.exampleCN: apt 是肯定词干。

items.example: Inept adds the negative prefix.
items.exampleCN: inept 加了否定前缀。

items.example: The suffix -itude forms ineptitude.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -itude 构成 ineptitude。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms ineptness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 ineptness。

items.meaning: to make fit for a purpose
items.example: Adapt keeps the fitting sense of apt.
items.exampleCN: adapt 保留 apt 的「相配」义。

items.meaning: natural ability to fit a task
items.example: Aptitude is the noun of apt.
items.exampleCN: aptitude 是 apt 的名词形式。

definition_zh: 不可逃避的；无法避免的；必然的；摆脱不掉的
definition_en: impossible to escape, avoid, or get away from
core_image: 一扇门被铁条从外面焊死，屋里的人怎么推也推不开
scene: 病房窗外下着雨，老人望着远处，知道这一关终究躲不过。For the old man in the ward, the coming operation was an inescapable fact.
sceneCN: 这里 inescapable 是「无法避免的」（第 1 个义项：注定要面对、躲不开的）；句意：对病房里的老人来说，即将到来的手术是一个无法回避的事实。

pos.zh: 不可逃避的；无法避免的；必然的

derivatives.zh: 基础词加副词后缀 -ly，义为「不可避免地」
过去罕见的变体拼写，现已基本废弃，与本词同义

senses.title: Impossible to avoid
senses.definition: impossible to prevent from happening or to get out of
senses.definitionCN: 不可能阻止其发生、也躲不开的
senses.example: The meeting was long, but going up the aisle was an inescapable duty.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼办得很长，但走上红毯却是一项无法推脱的义务。
senses.why: The prefix in- denies escape, so what stays outside the reach of escape is what must be faced.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 否定了「escape（逃脱）」，于是逃不出去的东西，就成了必须面对的东西。

senses.title: Certain and necessary
senses.definition: seeming to be certain to happen or to follow logically
senses.definitionCN: 看上去必然会发生，或在逻辑上必然推出的
senses.example: If costs keep rising, bankruptcy is the inescapable result.
senses.exampleCN: 如果成本持续上涨，破产就是必然的结果。
senses.why: Once something cannot be escaped, it stops being an option and becomes a necessity.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某件事逃不掉，它就不再是一种选择，而被看成必然。

senses.title: Always present and felt
senses.definition: present all the time and impossible to ignore or forget
senses.definitionCN: 始终存在且无法忽视或忘记的
senses.example: A restaurant helped people name the inescapable emptiness under the busy surface.
senses.exampleCN: 一家餐厅帮人们说出了忙碌表面之下那种摆脱不掉的空虚。
senses.why: An emotion or memory that cannot be escaped fills every hour, so the word spreads to feelings.
senses.whyCN: 逃不掉的情绪或记忆会占满每一刻，因此这个词也用于描述感受。

senses.title: Impossible to leave
senses.definition: from which a person cannot get away physically
senses.definitionCN: 人在身体上无法从中脱身的
senses.example: The narrow valley became an inescapable trap for the small team.
senses.exampleCN: 这条狭窄的山谷成了小队无法脱身的陷阱。
senses.why: This is the most literal use: a space closes in, and every exit is blocked.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的用法：空间收拢，所有出口都被堵死。

senses.title: Too strong to resist
senses.definition: so powerful that a person cannot resist or ignore the pull
senses.definitionCN: 力量强大到人无法抵抗或忽视的
senses.example: The pull of the tide felt slow and inescapable.
senses.exampleCN: 潮水的拉扯缓慢而不可抗拒。
senses.why: Resistance is also a kind of escape, so what cannot be resisted is described with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 抵抗也是一种「挣脱」，所以无法抵抗的东西也用同一个词来描述。

senses.title: Impossible to deny
senses.titleCN: 无法否认的；不可辩驳的
senses.definition: so clear in evidence that it cannot be denied or explained away
senses.definitionCN: 证据清楚到无法否认或搪塞过去的
senses.example: The lawyers faced an inescapable conclusion from the new documents.
senses.exampleCN: 面对新文件，律师们得出了一个无法辩驳的结论。
senses.why: Denying a fact is also trying to slip away from it, so airtight evidence is called inescapable.
senses.whyCN: 否认事实也是一种「溜走」，所以铁证如山的证据被称为 inescapable。

intro.en: Inescapable is a modern English formation: the Latin prefix in- meaning not, plus escape, which came into English from Old French eschaper, itself from Latin.
intro.cn: inescapable 是近代英语自己造的词：拉丁语否定前缀 in-（不）加上 escape；escape 经古法语 eschaper 传入英语，出自拉丁语。

items.en: The prefix in- means not, and ex- means out, and together with the root cap- they shape the idea of getting out.
items.cn: 拉丁语前缀 in- 意为「不」，ex- 意为「向外」，它们与词根 cap- 共同构成「脱身而出」的概念。

items.en: Excapare is a late popular form built from ex- and capa, the cloak, as if to slip out of a garment.
items.cn: 一般认为，俗拉丁语重构形式 excapare 由 ex- 与 capa（斗篷）组成，意象是像脱掉外套一样溜出去。

items.en: Eschaper means to get away, and its Old North French form escapes into English.
items.cn: 古法语 eschaper 意为脱身，其北方方言形式由此进入英语。

items.en: Escape becomes an English verb meaning to get free.
items.cn: escape 成为英语动词，意为逃脱。

items.en: Speakers attach the negative prefix in- to the adjective escapable to make inescapable, first recorded in the early nineteenth century.
items.cn: 使用者把否定前缀 in- 加在形容词 escapable 前面，造出 inescapable，一般认为首见于一八〇〇年代早期。

items.en: Inescapable spreads from descriptions of physical traps to arguments, emotions, and conclusions.
items.cn: 现代英语中，inescapable 从描写实体陷阱扩展到论点、情绪与结论。

note.en: Inescapable is escape with a negative in-; its neighbours include unavoidable and inevitable in meaning, and incapable and inevitable in spelling.
note.cn: inescapable 就是 escape 加上否定前缀 in-；在意义上与 unavoidable、inevitable 相邻，在拼写上要特别提防 incapable 与 inevitable。

entries.definition: possible to avoid or get away from
entries.definitionCN: 可逃避的；躲得开的；与 inescapable 只差否定前缀
无能力的；只是拼写相近，词源不同，capable 来自拉丁语 capax
难以置信的；只是拼写相近，词源不同，词根是拉丁语 credere
无法避免的；最中性的近义词，多用于事件
不可避免的；强调注定会发生

entries.definition: in a way that cannot be avoided
entries.definitionCN: 不可避免地；派生副词形式

normalIntro.en: Inescapable is built from two clear pieces: the negative in- and escape, so you can read it as not escapable.
normalIntro.cn: inescapable 由两块清楚的部件组成：否定前缀 in- 与 escape，可以读作「不可逃脱的」。

normal.en: Split it as in plus escape plus able: what cannot be escaped is inescapable.
normal.cn: 拆成 in + escape + able：逃不掉的，就是 inescapable。

normal.en: The adverb inescapably drops able and adds ly.
normal.cn: 副词 inescapably 就是去掉 able 再加 -ly。

normal.en: An inescapable fact is often paired with a verb of facing, such as face.
normal.cn: inescapable fact 常与 face 一类的动词搭配，表示「直面」。

normal.en: The usual conclusion collocation is inescapable conclusion, used in argument and law.
normal.cn: 常见搭配 inescapable conclusion 多用于论证与法律语境。

normal.en: Compare unavoidable: inescapable is more vivid and sounds slightly literary.
normal.cn: 对比 unavoidable：inescapable 画面感更强，也稍显文学化。

abstract.en: Picture a door welded shut from the outside.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门被从外面焊死。

abstract.en: Think of a shadow that keeps step with you down the street.
abstract.cn: 想象一道影子在街上始终跟着你的脚步。

abstract.en: Imagine a bill that arrives every month, no matter what.
abstract.cn: 想象一张无论如何每个月都会到的账单。

examples.en: Population growth makes urban expansion an inescapable trend.
examples.cn: 人口增长使城市扩张成为一种不可回避的趋势。

examples.en: He accepted the inescapable fact that the old farm would be sold.
examples.cn: 他接受了那座老农场终将被卖掉这一无法回避的事实。

examples.en: The burden of care fell inescapably on the youngest daughter.
examples.cn: 照护的重担不可避免地落在了最小的女儿身上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬是逃不走」——inescapable 读起来像「硬是 keep 不跑」，怎么挣扎都「逃」不出去；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ escape（拉丁语 ex- 向外 + capa 斗篷 → 俗拉丁语 excapare 脱身 → 古法语 eschaper → 英语 escape），构词为 in- + escapable，核心义「逃不出去」。

sensesIntro.en: Inescapable starts from the plain physical refusal of escape, then extends to necessity, to feelings that will not leave, and to facts that cannot be denied.
sensesIntro.cn: inescapable 从最直白的「身体上逃不出去」出发，再延伸到必然性、挥之不去的感受，以及无法否认的事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door welded shut, with no way out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇被焊死的门，没有出口。

branches.en: The basic sense simply denies escape.
branches.cn: 基本义就是否定一切逃脱。

branches.en: What cannot be escaped turns into what must happen.
branches.cn: 逃不掉的事情变成必然会发生的事情。

branches.en: A feeling that will not go away is inescapable too.
branches.cn: 挥之不去的感受同样是 inescapable。

branches.en: Both physical confinement and overpowering pull deny the person a way out.
branches.cn: 身体上的困禁与压倒性的吸引都让人无处可退。

branches.en: Denying evidence is a kind of slipping away, so airtight proof is called inescapable.
branches.cn: 否认证据是一种溜走，所以铁证也被称作 inescapable。

intro.en: Inescapable is a transparent modern compound of a negative prefix and a verb-like base, with a handful of English relatives built on escape.
intro.cn: inescapable 是结构清晰的近代合成词：否定前缀加上类似动词的词根，另有若干以 escape 为基础的英语同族词。

latinIntro.en: Escape goes back to Latin ex- out of, and a popular Latin form excapare, to slip out of one s cloak.
latinIntro.cn: escape 源于拉丁语 ex-（向外）以及俗拉丁语形式 excapare，意为从斗篷里脱身出来。

items.example: In- turns escapable into inescapable.
items.exampleCN: in- 把 escapable 变成 inescapable。

items.meaning: to get free from a place or situation
items.example: Escape is the base from which the adjective grows.
items.exampleCN: escape 是这个形容词的构词基础。

items.example: The suffix -able forms escapable from escape.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 使 escape 构成 escapable。

items.example: Escapable is the positive partner of the entry word.
items.exampleCN: escapable 是本词的正向对应形式。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms inescapably.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 inescapably。

items.meaning: in a way that cannot be avoided
items.example: Inescapably modifies verbs such as fall or follow.
items.exampleCN: inescapably 常修饰 fall、follow 一类动词。

items.example: The suffix -ness could form inescapableness, though it is rare.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 理论上可构成 inescapableness，但很少使用。

items.example: Escaped appears in phrases like an escaped prisoner.
items.exampleCN: escaped 见于 an escaped prisoner 这类搭配。

items.example: Escapism keeps the escape image and moves it into the mind.
items.exampleCN: escapism 保留「逃脱」的意象，把它移到了心理层面。

latinEntries.meaning: to slip out of a cloak
latinEntries.meaningCN: 从斗篷里挣脱出来（重构形式，一般认为）

definition_zh: 无法解释的；难以理解的；莫名其妙的
definition_en: impossible to explain, understand, or account for
core_image: 一把锁着的抽屉，钥匙在锁孔里怎么拧都不动，里面的东西始终看不见
scene: 老宅的阁楼上有一只木箱，纹路每夜都变，家里人谁也说不清缘由。The shifting pattern on the wooden box was quite inexplicable to all of them.
sceneCN: 这里 inexplicable 是「无法解释的」（第 1 个义项：说不出原因、讲不通的）；句意：那只木箱上不断变化的纹路，对他们所有人来说都完全无法解释。

pos.zh: 无法解释的；难以理解的；莫名其妙的

collocations.zh: 出于某种莫名其妙的原因

derivatives.zh: 基础词加副词后缀 -ly，义为「令人费解地；莫名其妙地」
基础词去 -e 加 -ability，义为「无法解释性」，较为生僻
去掉否定前缀 in- 后的对立词，义为「可以解释的」

senses.title: Impossible to explain
senses.definition: for which no reasonable explanation can be found or given
senses.definitionCN: 找不到、也给不出合理解释的
senses.example: The sudden power cut remains inexplicable to the engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 那次突然停电对工程师们来说仍然无法解释。
senses.why: In- denies the explicable, that is, what can be unfolded or made clear, so the fact stays folded up.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 否定了「可解释的」，即本来能展开讲清楚的东西，于是这件事就一直「叠着」打不开。

senses.title: Strange and baffling
senses.definition: so odd or eccentric that it puzzles and dismays people
senses.definitionCN: 古怪反常到令人困惑、不安的
senses.example: Her inexplicable fits of laughter worried the whole class.
senses.exampleCN: 她那些莫名其妙的阵发性大笑让全班都担心。
senses.why: When behaviour has no visible cause, observers experience it as an eerie strangeness rather than a plain gap in knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 当行为找不到可见的原因时，旁观者感到的不是「缺个答案」，而是一种怪异不安的气氛。

senses.title: Resistant to human knowledge
senses.definition: belonging to a matter that no human investigation can fully settle
senses.definitionCN: 属于人类任何探究都无法彻底弄清的事情
senses.example: The origin of the universe stays largely inexplicable to science.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙的起源在很大程度上仍是科学无法解释的。
senses.why: The same denial can be stretched from one puzzle to whole fields of knowledge that remain closed.
senses.whyCN: 同一个否定结构可以从单个谜题扩展到整片始终打不开的知识领域。

senses.title: Impossible to justify
senses.titleCN: 无从解释的；讲不出理由的
senses.definition: for which the person concerned cannot give any reason or defence
senses.definitionCN: 当事人自己说不出理由、也无法辩解的
senses.example: He gave an inexplicable excuse and then left the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他给了一个讲不出理由的借口，随后离开了房间。
senses.why: The word can also deny the speaker access to an account, making a reply that explains nothing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可以否定「说话人给出说法的能力」，所以它也能形容根本没解释什么的回答。

senses.title: Said of fate or mystery
senses.definition: described as beyond reason, often in a poetic or fearful tone
senses.definitionCN: 被描述为超越理性的，常带诗意或敬畏语气
senses.example: The island had an inexplicable hold on everyone who visited.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛对每个来访者都有一种神秘莫测的吸引力。
senses.why: Old uses of the word treat fate and mystery as things no explanation can ever reach.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的旧用法把命运与神秘归入一切解释都无法触及的范畴。

intro.en: Inexplicable joins the Latin negative prefix in- to the root plicare, to fold, which also yields explicare, to unfold or explain; the same root is visible in explicit, simple, and complex.
intro.cn: inexplicable 由拉丁语否定前缀 in- 与 plicare（折叠）构成，这个词根也见于 explicit、simple、complex 等词。

items.en: The root meaning to fold or plait lies at the base of Latin plicare.
items.cn: 一般认为，表示「折叠、编织」的古老词根是拉丁语 plicare 的来源。

items.en: Plicare means to fold, and explicare means to unfold, that is, to explain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 plicare 意为折叠，explicare 意为展开，也就是解释清楚。

items.en: Seneca uses inexplicabilis in the sense of not to be disentangled.
items.cn: 一般认为，塞内加在公元一世纪已使用 inexplicabilis，表示「解不开」之意。

items.en: The French form inexplicable passes the Latin adjective into early modern Europe.
items.cn: 一般认为，十六世纪的法语形式 inexplicable 把这个拉丁形容词带入近代欧洲语言。

items.en: Inexplicable enters English meaning unable to be unfolded or explained.
items.cn: inexplicable 进入英语，意为「无法展开、无法解释」。

items.en: The word grows into the familiar phrase for some inexplicable reason.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词发展出 for some inexplicable reason 这一常见说法。

note.en: Inexplicable shares its stem with explain and explicit; its near neighbours describe things that cannot be understood.
note.cn: inexplicable 与 explain、explicit 共享词根；它的近义词都表示「理解不了」。

entries.definitionCN: 可以解释的；去掉否定前缀 in- 后的对立词
明确的；同出拉丁语 explicare，本义「展开」
不可阻挡的；只是拼写相近，词源不同，词根是 exorare 劝服
无法解释的；最直白的同义表达
令人困惑的；强调让人不知所措
难以捉摸的；多形容神情或动机，比本词更正式

normalIntro.en: Inexplicable is built on the same Latin stem as explain: the word means that something cannot be unfolded, or made clear.
normalIntro.cn: inexplicable 与 explain 共用拉丁词根，意思是某件事没法「展开」、没法说清。

normal.en: Link inexplicable to explain: if something cannot be explained, it is inexplicable.
normal.cn: 把 inexplicable 与 explain 联系起来：解释不清的，就是 inexplicable。

normal.en: The root plicare means fold, so explicable is literally able to be unfolded.
normal.cn: 词根 plicare 意为折叠，所以 explicable 字面上就是「能展开的」。

normal.en: The fixed phrase for some inexplicable reason often opens a sentence.
normal.cn: 固定短语 for some inexplicable reason 常放在句首。

normal.en: The adverb inexplicably is very frequent and often sits before a verb.
normal.cn: 副词 inexplicably 使用频率很高，常放在动词前。

normal.en: Compare explicit, which keeps the same stem but means clearly stated.
normal.cn: 对比 explicit：词根相同，但意思是「明说的」。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer whose contents you can never see.
abstract.cn: 想象一只你永远看不见内容的抽屉。

abstract.en: Think of a map with one region left blank on purpose.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图上有一块被刻意留白的区域。

abstract.en: Imagine a door that has a keyhole but no key anywhere.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇有锁孔却根本找不到钥匙的门。

examples.en: For some inexplicable reason, the dog refused to enter the house.
examples.cn: 不知什么原因，那只狗死活不肯进屋。

examples.en: The disappearance of the ship remains inexplicable to this day.
examples.cn: 那艘船的失踪至今仍无法解释。

examples.en: Inexplicably, the machine started working again after a night in the cold.
examples.cn: 莫名其妙的是，机器在冷处搁了一夜后又能运转了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一宁可不说了」——inexplicable 听起来像「因不解释而可……」，一连串「说不清、解释不了」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ explicare（展开、解释，源于 plicare 折叠）→ 后期拉丁语 inexplicabilis（解不开的）→ 法语 inexplicable → 英语，核心义「展不开、讲不清」。

sensesIntro.en: Inexplicable moves from a missing explanation, to odd and eerie behaviour, to whole fields that no human account can reach, and finally to fate and mystery.
sensesIntro.cn: inexplicable 从「缺少解释」出发，转指古怪诡异的行为，再扩展到人类无法抵达的知识领域，最后落向命运与神秘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a locked drawer that no key opens.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只没有钥匙能打开的抽屉。

branches.en: The plain sense states that no explanation can be given.
branches.cn: 基本义就是「给不出解释」。

branches.en: Next the word colours behaviour as odd and dismaying.
branches.cn: 接着，这个词把行为染上古怪而不安的色彩。

branches.en: The denial stretches over whole fields of unsolved knowledge.
branches.cn: 这种否定延伸到整片尚未解开的领域。

branches.en: Both a puzzling event and a reasonless excuse fail to explain anything.
branches.cn: 费解的事件与说不上理由的借口，都等于什么都没解释。

branches.en: Fate and mystery are the points where explanation gives way to awe.
branches.cn: 命运与神秘是解释让位于敬畏的地方。

intro.en: Inexplicable is a Latin-derived adjective with a productive negative prefix and a suffix shared by hundreds of English words.
intro.cn: inexplicable 是拉丁来源的形容词，带有能产的否定前缀，以及一个在英语中构成大量词的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin plicare, to fold, yields explicare, to unfold or explain, and the adjective inexplicabilis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 plicare（折叠）产生 explicare（展开、解释），并由此构成形容词 inexplicabilis。

items.example: In- forms the negative of explicable.
items.exampleCN: in- 构成 explicable 的否定形式。

items.example: Ex- in explicare carries the sense of unfolding outward.
items.exampleCN: explicare 中的 ex- 带有「向外展开」的含义。

items.example: Plicare supplies the folded image behind the word.
items.exampleCN: plicare 提供了这个词背后「折叠」的意象。

items.example: The suffix -able builds explicable and inexplicable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 explicable 与 inexplicable。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms inexplicably.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 inexplicably。

items.meaning: in a way that cannot be explained
items.example: Inexplicably often stands at the start of a clause.
items.exampleCN: inexplicably 常放在从句开头。

items.example: The suffix -ability forms inexplicability, rarely used.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ability 构成极少使用的 inexplicability。

items.meaningCN: 简单的；单一的（拉丁语 simplex）
items.example: Simplex also carries the folding root plicare.
items.exampleCN: simplex 同样带有「折叠」词根 plicare。

items.example: Duplex pairs the root with duo, two.
items.exampleCN: duplex 把该词根与 duo（二）组合在一起。

definition_zh: 不会犯错的；万无一失的；绝对可靠的；一贯正确的
core_image: 一台老式天平，放上任何砝码都稳稳回正，从不倾斜
scene: 试验台上摆着一套老式仪器，工程师们反复校准，宣称它从不失手。The technicians trusted the new device because it seemed infallible in every trial.
sceneCN: 这里 infallible 是「不会出错的」（第 1 个义项：在判断或行动上从不犯错）；句意：技术人员信任这台新设备，因为它在每次试验中似乎都不会出错。

pos.zh: 不会犯错的；万无一失的；绝对可靠的
不会犯错的人（古旧用法，今罕用）

derivatives.zh: 基础词加副词后缀 -ly，义为「万无一失地；必定」
基础词去 -e 加 -ibility，义为「不会出错的性质」，宗教与政论文献中常见
去掉否定前缀 in- 后的对立形容词，义为「会犯错的」

senses.title: Incapable of error
senses.titleCN: 不会犯错的；一贯正确的
senses.definition: never making a mistake in judgement or action
senses.definitionCN: 在判断或行动上从不犯错的
senses.example: No coach is infallible, however many titles he has won.
senses.exampleCN: 没有哪位教练是不会犯错的，无论他赢过多少冠军。
senses.why: In- denies fallible, which comes from Latin fallere, to deceive or slip up, so an infallible person cannot be fooled or slip.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 否定了 fallible（会犯错的），后者源于拉丁语 fallere（欺骗、使失足），所以 infallible 就是骗不住、也踏不空的人。

senses.title: Sure to work
senses.titleCN: 万无一失的；必定奏效的
senses.definition: certain to succeed or to produce the intended result
senses.definitionCN: 必定成功或产生预期结果的
senses.example: There is no infallible remedy for a bad night of sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 对一夜没睡好这件事，并没有什么万无一失的良方。
senses.why: If a method never slips up, it is described as sure to work, so the person sense and the method sense share one image.
senses.whyCN: 方法如果从不「失手」，就叫必定奏效，所以「人」与「方法」两个义项共用同一个意象。

senses.title: Entirely reliable
senses.definition: so dependable that it never fails or lets people down
senses.definitionCN: 可靠到从不出岔子、从不让人失望的
senses.example: Her infallible memory for dates saved the family archive.
senses.exampleCN: 她对日期从不出错的记忆力救下了家族的档案。
senses.why: The word often points less at never being wrong than at never failing in a supporting role.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常用于强调「从不掉链子」，而不只是「从不出错」，多形容可依赖的能力或物件。

senses.title: Named in religion
senses.definition: used of a doctrine or a teacher whose teaching is held to be free of error
senses.definitionCN: 用于教义或教师，指其教导被认为不含错误的
senses.example: The council debated whether papal statements were infallible.
senses.exampleCN: 会议争论教皇的声明是否具有无谬误性。
senses.why: Old theological use turned the absence of error into a formal claim about doctrine.
senses.whyCN: 古代神学用法把「无错」变成了针对教义的正式主张，而不只是普通的可靠。

senses.title: Said ironically
senses.definition: describing a plan or person that is presented as flawless but plainly is not
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个被说成完美无缺、实则显而易见有问题的人或计划
senses.example: His infallible plan collapsed on the very first day.
senses.exampleCN: 他那个「万无一失」的计划第一天就崩了。
senses.why: Because in- is absolute, piling the word on a human plan invites irony and marks overconfidence.
senses.whyCN: 因为 in- 表示绝对否定，把它加在人的计划上就天然带讽刺，常用来暗示过分自信。

intro.en: Infallible is built on the Latin verb fallere, to deceive or trip up, and the adjective fallibilis; the negative prefix in- closes the door on slipping.
intro.cn: infallible 建立在拉丁语动词 fallere（欺骗、使失足）与形容词 fallibilis 之上，否定前缀 in- 把「失足」这扇门关上了。

items.en: A root meaning to stumble has been reconstructed behind Latin fallere, though the reconstruction is disputed.
items.cn: 一般认为，学者在拉丁语 fallere 背后重构出表示「绊倒」的词根，但这一重构仍有争议。

items.en: Fallere means to deceive or to cause to slip, and fallibilis means deceivable.
items.cn: 拉丁语 fallere 意为欺骗或使人失足，fallibilis 意为可被蒙骗的。

items.en: Infallibilis appears in later Latin in the sense of not able to be deceived.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语中已见 infallibilis，意为不会被蒙骗的。

items.en: Theologians use the term for teaching that cannot mislead.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语的神学家把该词用于不会误导人的教导。

items.en: Infallible enters English and spreads from doctrine to medicine and everyday advice.
items.cn: 英语首次记录的用法出现在十六世纪，此后从教义扩展到医学与日常建议。

items.en: The word becomes common in the ironical phrase an infallible plan.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词在 an infallible plan 这类讽刺说法里十分常见。

note.en: Infallible shares its Latin base with fail and fallacy; its near neighbours all stress certainty or exemption from error.
note.cn: infallible 与 fail、fallacy 共享拉丁语词基；它的近义词都在强调「确定」与「免于出错」。

entries.definitionCN: 会犯错的；去掉否定前缀 in- 后的对立词
谬见；谬误；同出拉丁语 fallere，词根相同
不可行的；只是拼写相近，词源不同，feasible 来自古法语 faire
完美无瑕的；强调没有瑕疵
无误差的；极为准确的，常形容眼光或直觉

entries.definition: the quality of never being wrong
entries.definitionCN: 不会出错的性质；派生名词

normalIntro.en: Infallible is in plus fallible, and fallible is the twin of fail: whoever cannot fall cannot fail.
normalIntro.cn: infallible 就是 in 加 fallible；fallible 与 fail 同源，从不「跌倒」的人自然也就不会失败。

normal.en: Split it as in plus fall plus ible, and link fall to fail by the shared idea of slipping.
normal.cn: 拆成 in + fall + ible，并用「失足」的意思把 fall 与 fail 联系起来。

normal.en: The noun is infallibility, formed with the suffix -ibility.
normal.cn: 名词是 infallibility，由词尾 -ibility 构成。

normal.en: The phrase by no means infallible is a quick way to admit that someone can be wrong.
normal.cn: by no means infallible 是承认某人也会出错的快捷表达。

normal.en: Infallible is often used ironically, as in his infallible plan.
normal.cn: infallible 常用于反讽，比如 his infallible plan。

normal.en: Compare flawless: flawless concerns defects, infallible concerns mistakes in judgement or action.
normal.cn: 对比 flawless：flawless 强调瑕疵，infallible 强调判断或行动上的错误。

abstract.en: Picture a balance scale that always returns to level.
abstract.cn: 想象一台天平，永远回到水平。

abstract.en: Think of a guidebook whose map is always right.
abstract.cn: 想象一本地图永远正确的旅行指南。

abstract.en: Imagine a doctor who never misreads a chart.
abstract.cn: 想象一位从不会看错病历的医生。

examples.en: The professor warns that no theory is infallible.
examples.cn: 教授提醒说，没有哪种理论是不会出错的。

examples.en: Good grammar is not an infallible guide to clear writing.
examples.cn: 语法正确并不是写出清楚文字的万无一失的指南。

examples.en: She picked her way through the crowd with infallible instinct.
examples.cn: 她凭着从不出错的直觉穿过人群。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因罚力薄」——infallible 听起来像「再怎么罚也扳不倒」，怎么打击都不出错；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ fallere（欺骗、使失足）→ fallibilis（可被蒙骗的）→ 后期拉丁语 infallibilis → 英语，核心义「不会失足、骗不倒」。

sensesIntro.en: Infallible begins with a person who never errs, widens to sure methods and dependable powers, then narrows into a doctrinal claim before ending in irony.
sensesIntro.cn: infallible 从「不会犯错的人」开始，扩大到「必定奏效的方法」与「可靠的能力」，随后收窄为宗教教义意义上的断言，最后落入反讽。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance that always returns to level.
core.cn: 核心意象：永远回到水平的天平。

branches.en: A person who cannot slip is the first sense.
branches.cn: 不会失足的人，是最初的义项。

branches.en: A method that cannot slip is sure to work.
branches.cn: 不会失手的方法，就是必定奏效。

branches.en: What never fails becomes wholly dependable.
branches.cn: 从不失败的东西，就成了完全可靠的依靠。

branches.en: Religion turns the absence of error into a formal claim.
branches.cn: 宗教把「无错」变成了正式的教义主张。

branches.en: The absolute prefix invites irony when it meets human plans.
branches.cn: 这个绝对化的否定前缀一旦遇上人的计划，就带上了讽刺。

intro.en: Infallible is a Latin negative prefix added to a Latin adjective, with a productive adverb, noun, and opposite in English.
intro.cn: infallible 是拉丁语否定前缀加在拉丁语形容词上的合成词，英语中另有能产的副词、名词与反义词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fallere, to deceive, yields fallibilis and later infallibilis, the direct source of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fallere（欺骗）产生 fallibilis，后来又产生 infallibilis，后者是英语这个词的直接来源。

items.example: In- negates fallible to make the entry word.
items.exampleCN: in- 否定 fallible，构成本词。

items.meaning: to deceive, to trip someone up
items.example: Fallere supplies the trap-like image of slipping.
items.exampleCN: fallere 提供「失足」的圈套意象。

items.example: The suffix -ible forms fallible from the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ible 从拉丁词干构成 fallible。

items.example: Fallible is the positive partner of the entry word.
items.exampleCN: fallible 是本词的正向对应形式。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms infallibly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 infallibly。

items.example: The suffix -ibility forms infallibility.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ibility 构成 infallibility。

items.example: Fail shares the slipping root with the entry word.
items.exampleCN: fail 与本词共享「失足」词根。

items.example: Fallacy also comes from Latin fallere.
items.exampleCN: fallacy 同样来自拉丁语 fallere。

items.example: False is related through the same Latin root.
items.exampleCN: false 通过同一个拉丁词根与本词相关。

latinEntries.example: Fallere is the stem behind fail, fallacy, and infallible.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fallere 是 fail、fallacy 与 infallible 共有的词干。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 不会被蒙骗的；不会出错的
latinEntries.example: Infallibilis is the direct source of the entry word.
latinEntries.exampleCN: infallibilis 是本词在拉丁语中的直接来源。

definition_zh: 传染力；感染力；致病传播能力
definition_en: the ability of a pathogen to enter a host and start an infection
core_image: 一颗病毒粒子推开细胞的门，把遗传物质塞了进去
scene: 实验室里，研究员比较两种病毒株的传染力。In the lab, the researchers compared the infectivity of the two virus strains.
sceneCN: 这里 infectivity 是「传染力」（第 1 个义项：病原体侵入宿主并建立感染的能力）；句意：在实验室里，研究员比较了两种病毒株的传染力。

pos.zh: 传染力；感染力
感染性；致病性（物质或样本）

derivatives.zh: 由 -ive 构成的形容词，义为「有传染性的；能感染的」
由 -ious 构成的形容词，义为「传染的；有感染力的」
传染；感染，是整组词的核心动词
由 -tion 构成的名词，义为「感染；传染病」

senses.title: The power of a pathogen to infect
senses.definition: the capacity of a virus, bacterium, or other agent to enter a host and establish an infection
senses.definitionCN: 病毒、细菌或其他病原体侵入宿主并建立感染的能力
senses.example: The variant shows enhanced infectivity in crowded places.
senses.exampleCN: 这种变异株在拥挤场所表现出更强的传染力。
senses.why: The adjective infective means able to infect, and -ity turns that ability into a measurable property.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 infective 表示「能传染的」，后缀 -ity 把这种能力变成一个可以度量的属性，于是有了「传染力」。

senses.title: Contagious power over a population
senses.titleCN: 人群中的传播力；感染力
senses.definition: the tendency of an infection to pass quickly from person to person within a group
senses.definitionCN: 一种感染在人群中迅速人传人的倾向
senses.example: Public-health teams track infectivity when schools reopen.
senses.exampleCN: 学校复课时，公共卫生团队会追踪传播力。
senses.why: Once -ity names a property, it can also describe how a bug behaves across a whole population.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 -ity 指代一种属性，它也能描述病原体在整个群体中的行为，所以从单个个体扩展到了人群层面。

senses.title: The infectious quality of a substance
senses.definition: the degree to which a sample, tissue, or waste can still transmit infection
senses.definitionCN: 样本、组织或废弃物仍能传播感染的程度
senses.example: Laboratory waste is tested for infectivity before disposal.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室废弃物在处理前会检测其感染性。
senses.why: The property sense extends from living hosts to any material that carries a living agent.
senses.whyCN: 「属性」义项从活的宿主扩展到任何携带活病原体的物质，于是废物、组织、血样也谈感染性。

senses.title: The sense in which a bug can be caught
senses.titleCN: 可被感染的特性（与传染性相对）
senses.definition: the susceptibility of an agent to being infected, as opposed to its power to infect
senses.definitionCN: 病原体自身被感染的可能性，与它传染别人的能力相对
senses.example: Some parasites have low infectivity to their own kind.
senses.exampleCN: 有些寄生物对同类几乎没有感染性。
senses.why: In technical writing the -ity noun can flip direction: an agent may be the one that can be infected.
senses.whyCN: 在技术文献里，这个 -ity 名词可以换个方向：病原体也可能是「被感染」的一方，这时译作可被感染的特性。

senses.title: Power to spread by words or images
senses.definition: the figurative ability of an idea, joke, or image to spread from mind to mind
senses.definitionCN: 观点、笑话或图像在头脑之间传播的比喻性能力
senses.example: The infectivity of a good slogan is hard to measure.
senses.exampleCN: 好口号的感染力很难衡量。
senses.why: The metaphor of a bug passing between hosts is borrowed to describe how catchy ideas travel.
senses.whyCN: 把病原体在宿主之间传播的比喻借过来，就可以形容那些朗朗上口的观点如何在人群中扩散。

senses.title: A score used in virus assays
senses.definition: the value a laboratory reports when it measures how many particles can infect living cells
senses.definitionCN: 实验室测量有多少颗粒能感染活细胞时报告出的数值
senses.example: The drug lowered the measured infectivity by eighty percent.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药物使测得的感染性数值下降了八成。
senses.why: From the property sense, laboratories turn infectivity into a number printed on a report.
senses.whyCN: 在属性义项的基础上，实验室进一步把这个属性变成报告上的具体数值，于是有了测定值。

intro.en: Infectivity is built on the Latin verb inficere, to stain or taint, with the adjective infective and the suffix -ity.
intro.cn: infectivity 建立在拉丁语动词 inficere（染上、玷污）之上，由形容词 infective 加后缀 -ity 构成。

items.en: Inficere means to taint or stain something by mixing another thing into it.
items.cn: inficere 意为把另一样东西混进去，使某物染上或蒙污。

items.en: The medical sense of infecting the body with disease appears in later medical Latin.
items.cn: 「使身体染病」的医学义在中世纪后期的医学拉丁语中出现。

items.en: The verb infect enters English meaning to taint or contaminate.
items.cn: 动词 infect 进入英语，意为染污、污染。

items.en: Infective appears as an adjective meaning able to infect.
items.cn: 形容词 infective 出现，意为「能传染的」。

items.en: Infectivity is coined as the noun of property, following the Latin -itas pattern.
items.cn: infectivity 按拉丁语 -itas 的模式造出，用作表示属性的名词。

items.en: Epidemiology makes infectivity a routine measurement of viral behaviour.
items.cn: 现代流行病学把 infectivity 变成描述病毒行为的常规测量指标。

note.en: Infectivity sits among infect, infective, infection, and the family of biological properties that also claim influence over disease.
note.cn: infectivity 处在 infect、infective、infection 这一词族之中，也和一组同样描述疾病影响力的生物学属性词相邻。

entries.definitionCN: 能引起感染的；有传染性的
感染；传染病

entries.definition: spreading from one person to another
entries.definitionCN: 传染的；易传播的

entries.definition: the degree of harm a pathogen can cause
entries.definitionCN: 致病力；毒力（与传染力不同，强调伤害程度）

entries.definition: the ease with which a disease passes between people
entries.definitionCN: 传染性；传播的容易程度

entries.definition: the ability of an organism to cause disease
entries.definitionCN: 致病性；引发疾病的能力

normalIntro.en: Infectivity is the property noun of the infect family: a virus that proves it can enter cells and start trouble.
normalIntro.cn: infectivity 是 infect 词族的属性名词，指病毒已证明能进入细胞并引发问题的能力。

normal.en: Infect plus -ive gives infective, able to infect.
normal.cn: infect 加 -ive 得 infective，意为能传染的。

normal.en: Infective plus -ity gives infectivity, the property of being able to infect.
normal.cn: infective 加 -ity 得 infectivity，即「能传染」这一属性。

normal.en: The same -ity appears in activity and sensitivity, turning adjectives into property nouns.
normal.cn: 同一个 -ity 也见于 activity 和 sensitivity，它把形容词变成属性名词。

normal.en: Keep infectivity apart from virulence: infectivity is how easily it spreads, virulence is how badly it hurts.
normal.cn: 把 infectivity 与 virulence 分开：前者讲多容易传播，后者讲伤害有多重。

normal.en: Collocations pair it with high, low, and measure, as in high infectivity and measure the infectivity.
normal.cn: 常见搭配用 high、low、measure，例如高传染力、测定传染力。

abstract.en: Picture a virus particle pushing open a cell door and getting in.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗病毒粒子推开门，钻进了细胞。

abstract.en: Picture a sneeze in a crowded bus, reaching row after row.
abstract.cn: 想象拥挤公交车上的一声喷嚏，一排接一排地波及。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed lab bag labelled with a warning and a measured number.
abstract.cn: 想象一只贴着警示标志和测量数值的密封实验袋。

examples.en: High infectivity helps a virus spread long before its hosts show symptoms.
examples.cn: 高传染力使病毒在宿主出现症状之前就大量扩散。

examples.en: Freezing does not always reduce the infectivity of a sample.
examples.cn: 冷冻并不总能降低样本的感染性。

examples.en: The team tested how infectivity changes with temperature.
examples.cn: 研究团队测试了传染力如何随温度变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因费可提位体」——病原体「因」为「费」了力气才「可」以「提」高地在人「体」里占「位」，记住了传染力；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 inficere（混入、染污）→ infection / infect（感染）→ infective（能传染的）→ infect + -ive + -ity，核心义为「使某物染上外来之物，从而能继续传给下一个」。

sensesIntro.en: Infectivity starts as a pathogen s power to infect, widens to population spread and contaminated materials, then turns into a laboratory score and a metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: infectivity 先指病原体侵入宿主的能力，再扩展到人群传播与被污染物质，最后成为实验室数值和比喻用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a particle that pushes into a cell and starts a chain of copies.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗颗粒钻进细胞，开始复制链条。

branches.en: The basic sense is a pathogen s power to infect a host.
branches.cn: 基础义项是病原体侵入宿主的能力。

branches.en: The population sense asks how fast it moves between people.
branches.cn: 人群义项关心它在人之间传播得多快。

branches.en: The property can belong to a material or point back at the agent itself.
branches.cn: 这种属性可以属于物质，也可以反过来指向病原体自身。

branches.en: The metaphor moves from germs to slogans and images.
branches.cn: 比喻义从病菌挪到了口号和图像上。

branches.en: The laboratory score is the basic sense turned into a number.
branches.cn: 测定值把基础义项变成了一个数字。

intro.en: Infectivity is a four-part word family: infect, infection, infective, and the -ity noun that names the property.
intro.cn: infectivity 属于四件套词族：infect、infection、infective，以及用 -ity 命名该属性的名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin inficere, to taint, gives the verb; -ivus and -itas are the Latin adjective and noun endings that shape the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inficere（玷污）提供动词，拉丁语形容词词尾 -ivus 与名词词尾 -itas 塑造了其余部分。

items.example: The prefix in- puts something inside.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 表示把东西放进去。

items.example: Facere supplies the make part of the Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: facere 提供拉丁语动词中「使」的部分。

items.example: Inficere literally means to put something in.
items.exampleCN: inficere 字面义为把东西放进去。
